newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Canada urges China to hold swift elections in HK.
newsitem.headline: Canada urges China to hold swift elections in HK.

text.p: Canada urged China on Monday to hold an election in Hong Kong as soon as possible after Beijing resumes control of the British-ruled territory next July 1.

The Canadian message, which was faxed to media, was Ottawa's first official reaction to China's appointment last Saturday of a highly controversial 60-member assembly to replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council next July 1.

"An early replacement of the provisional legislature by an elected legislature based on democratic principles will significantly advance international confidence in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region," Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said in a statement issued by the Canadian Commission in Hong Kong.
Canada hoped the interim assembly would deal only with urgent matters essential to effect a smooth transition of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty at midnight next June 30, he said.
Canada has been watching the British colony's transition to Chinese rule with great concern, as more than 30,000 Canadian citizens reside in the colony.
